newsitem.title: USA: Orange & Rockland sets July rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Orange & Rockland sets July rate cuts.

text.p: Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc said Tuesday it has agreed to rate cuts beginning about July 1 as part of a four-year transition to a competitive power market.

The utility said the settlement agreement with the state Public Service Commission staff, the New York State Department of Economic Development, the Industrial Users Association and the National Association of Energy Services Companies would create $37 million in cumulative benefits for O&R customers over the four years.
The benefits would be attained chiefly through rate cuts.
The agreement calls for Orange & Rockland to expand its PowerPick energy-supplier choice program to include all customers about one year from now, the utility said.

That's unchanged from the company's October 1 proposal which also called for a rate freeze through the end of the century and perhaps beyond and functional separation of generation this year. That filing served as a basis for this agreement.
The pact also allows O&R to retain all earnings up to an 11.5 percent return on equity.

Above that level, the company said, 25 percent of earnings will be credited to customers, 50 percent to write down generation assets or be credited to customers and 25 percent will be retained by shareholders.

The company said it has agreed -- subject to shareholder and regulatory approval -- to be restructured into a regulated enegy distribution company, and unregulated energy production and energy service companies.
O&R said the agreement authorizes it to invest $25 million to develop unregulated companies such as energy services and marketing, telecommunications, and environmental projects.

The company said a portion of its existing rates would be designated as a Competitive Transition Charge to cover the costs of regulatory assets and generation assets with above market values. Spokesman Michael Donovan declined to estimate the amount of these assets.
The company said the charge would would remain in place for four years once retail competition begins.
At that time, the generation assets would be subject to a one-time final market valuation procedure to be developed.
The difference between the market and book values, as determined at that time, would be shared on a 80 percent for customers, 20 percent for shareholders basis, it said.
In October, O&R proposed an eight year transition charge.
The utility said its largest industrial customers could realize price reductions, composed of rate reductions and PowerPick savings, of as high as 12 percent as early as July.
This allows them to realize a price of $0.06 per kilowatt hour which is the national average, O&R said.

Other customers would realize a 2 percent direct rate reduction over the first two years of the plan -- 1 percent each year, it said. They could save an additional 3 to 5 percent by taking advantage of PowerPick, it added.
